A single Microsoft 365 data store gives the Gemini Enterprise assistant access to SharePoint, OneDrive, Excel, Outlook mail, calendars, contacts, and tasks, Microsoft Teams, and Microsoft Entra users and groups, so you don't need a separate data store for each product. BigQuery Feature Lakehouse supports BigQuery row-level security and column-level security with\\ dynamic data masking on Apache Iceberg tables in the Lakehouse runtime catalog ( GA). You can restrict which rows principals can see and mask sensitive column values by managing these policies with GoogleSQL DDL statements in BigQuery. On catalogs that use credential vending mode, the Apache Iceberg REST catalog endpoint vends storage credentials only to principals that have unmasked access to every protected column and, if the table has row-level access policies, unfiltered row access. Gemini Enterprise Feature Gemini Enterprise: Gemini 4 Neon available in web app, mobile app, Workflow Builder, and AI developer tools Gemini 4 Neon is generally available (GA) for the Gemini Enterprise web app, mobile app, Workflow Builder, and AI developer tools. - Location availability: Supported in global, us, and eu multi-regions, with data residency and ML processing support in us and eu. For unsupported in-country regions, you must confirm the warning dialog to route traffic to the global endpoint. For more information, see Data residency for Gemini\\ Enterprise. - App availability: Turned off by default. To make Gemini 4 Neon available to users, an administrator must turn on the model. For more information, see Manage features on the web\\ app. - Workflow Builder: Gemini 4 Neon is available in Workflow Builder for agent flow nodes and no-code agents. For more information, see Workflow\\ Builder. - AI developer tools: Enabled by default for licensed users when Antigravity authorized models uses the default selection. If your organization specifies a custom model list, an administrator must manually select Gemini 4 Neon. For more information, see Configure AI\\ developer tools\\ settings. Describe an app, dashboard, or prototype in chat, and Canvas generates a working, interactive single-page app as a single self-contained HTML file, with no code required. Users have the ability to create, preview, edit and export and share the generated HTML. This feature is generally available (GA). Actions run with the permissions of the user who authorized the connector. For more information, see the supported actions for the following connectors: - Google Calendar - Google Chat - Google Drive - Gmail Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Feature Gemini 4 Neon (GA) Gemini 4 Neon (gemini-4-neon) is generally available (GA) in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. Gemini 4 Neon is a Google Frontier Model subject to Section 34 of the Service Specific Terms (for details, see Abuse monitoring) and delivers high-performance coding, multi-step reasoning, and multimodal understanding at low latency for agentic enterprise workflows: - Unified 1,048,576-token limit and long decodes: Supports a unified 1,048,576-token input and output limit, where output includes thinking, function calls, and the final response. Single foreground segments generate up to 65,536 output tokens for streaming and non-streaming requests. Long decodes (continuationtoken) extend output up to 1,048,576 tokens (minus input tokens) on the Interactions\\ API and GenerateContent (v1beta1). The Interactions API also supports asynchronous server-managed background execution (background=true). - Thinking levels (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, and XHIGH): Supports four thinking levels, with HIGH as the default and XHIGH for deep reasoning workloads. Setting thinkingbudget or thinkinglevel="MINIMAL" returns an HTTP 400 validation error. - Implicit context caching with durable caching: Supports automatic implicit context caching with durable caching enabled by default for shared prompt prefixes of 4,096 tokens or more (explicit context caching isn't supported). - Cache write control and pricing: Starting on January 12, 2027, Gemini 4 Hydrogen and later models support cache control features with TTL configuration. You choose what to cache and how long cached content stays valid through TTL configuration. Cache writes are billed at 1.25x the standard input token price by default, and longer retention costs more. For details, see Gemini 4 pricing. - Office and OpenDocument file inputs: Supports Microsoft Office (.docx, .dotx, .doc, .pptx, .ppt, .xlsx, .xls) and OpenDocument (.odt, .odp, .ods) files inline or from Cloud Storage (gs://), including inside multimodal FunctionResponse parts. - Capabilities, consumption options, and endpoints: Available on the global endpoint and in the us and eu multi-regions across GenerateContent, the Interactions API, and the OpenAI compatibility Chat Completions API. Supports function calling, code execution, computer use, URL context, and Agentic video understanding. Grounding options include Grounding with Google Search, Google Maps, Web Grounding for Enterprise, and Parallel and Exa Web Search. Consumption options include Standard PayGo with Usage Tiers, Priority PayGo, Off-peak PayGo, batch inference, and Provisioned Throughput. For model specifications, code examples, and migration guidance from Gemini 3 models, see Gemini 4 Neon, the developer's guide to Gemini 4\\ Neon, and Get\\ started with Gemini\\ 4. Google Kubernetes Engine Issue In GKE versions 1.35, 1.36, and 1.37, enabling application-layer secrets encryption on a new or existing cluster whose control plane stores cluster state in Spanner encrypts only Kubernetes Secrets (ENCRYPTED) instead of all Kubernetes API objects (ALLOBJECTSENCRYPTIONENABLED). - Clusters that already have encryption of all Kubernetes API objects enabled (ALLOBJECTSENCRYPTIONENABLED) continue to encrypt all objects. - Clusters where application-layer secrets encryption is in the ENCRYPTED state encrypt only Secrets and require manual Secret re-encryption after a Cloud KMS key rotation. A fix to restore encryption of all Kubernetes API objects for newly configured clusters is in progress. You can use GKE Granular NAT to control outbound traffic and assign dedicated egress source IP addresses at the Kubernetes namespace level using the CloudNATGateway and TrafficSelector custom resources. Instead of applying a single NAT policy to an entire cluster, you can route egress traffic from specific namespaces through dedicated external IP addresses for Public NAT or dedicated subnet IP address ranges for Private NAT, without managing custom proxy instances. For more information, see About GKE Granular NAT and Configure GKE Granular NAT. Spanner Feature QueryData generates Graph Query Language (GQL) queries from natural language questions about your Spanner Graph property graphs. Your AI agent and LLM applications can explore connected data without writing GQL. Specify graphids in your request to generate GQL, and use optional context sets to improve accuracy. This feature is available in Preview. For more information, see QueryData overview.
